title: Guru Angad: humility
hook: the second Guru's light: the humble disciple who became the Guru
tomorrow: the emperor came to see the Guru. where did he have to sit?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Guru Nanak: wonder, the sky as the platter, already lit. Today his light passes on, and the clue is in a kitchen.

Steam, the clank of steel trays, and the smell of rice cooking slowly in milk. Simran is at the gurdwara langar on dish duty, sleeves pushed up, hands red from hot water, and she's been at it for hours. Up front, people are thanking the cooks. Nobody is thanking the sink. She sends you a photo of a mountain of pots. So how does a disciple become the Guru? Not by a contest. By the work nobody photographs.
screen: `STEAM, STEEL, RICE IN MILK.` → `NOBODY THANKS THE SINK.` → `THE WORK NOBODY PHOTOGRAPHS.`

segments.voice: Tradition remembers a man named Lehna, who came to Guru Nanak at Kartarpur and stayed to serve. The stories told about him are small and muddy: carrying a bundle of wet grass on his head, in his good clothes, because it needed carrying; doing the jobs others in the household thought beneath them. When the time came, Guru Nanak placed the Guruship on Lehna and named him Angad. A hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib by the bards Satta and Balvand says it simply. In paraphrase: the light was the same, the way was the same; only the body changed. That same hymn keeps a smell and a taste. It names Guru Angad's wife, Mata Khivi, a good woman who gave shade to all like a leafy tree, and in her langar, kheer, rice pudding, rich with ghee. One to tell a friend tonight: the Sikh scripture remembers a woman by the rice pudding she served. And Guru Nanak gives the word for what Lehna had, in Asa di Var: sweetness and humility are the essence of every virtue. Not thinking little of yourself. Sweetness, and a low place, chosen. Simran keeps scrubbing. A kid from the youth group picks up a towel beside her and doesn't say a word.
screen: `LEHNA, AND THE WET GRASS.` · `ONLY THE BODY CHANGED.` · `MATA KHIVI'S KHEER.` · `SWEETNESS AND HUMILITY.` · then, large: `HUMILITY.`

segments.voice: If there's a cup, a dish or a counter near you, wash or wipe it slowly by hand, one someone else would otherwise have to do. Feel the warmth of the water and notice the smell of the soap. Don't mention it to anyone afterward; let it stay quiet.
Guru Angad: the second Guru, once Lehna, the disciple who did the work nobody saw. Same light, a new body.
Hold onto this: humility, sweetness and a low place, chosen. Same light, new hands, old pots.

howItsDone: Sikhs remember Guru Angad as the disciple Lehna who served Guru Nanak; Sikhs serve in the langar by cooking, serving and washing up, and the scrubbing of dishes is a common first seva for young people.

fork.setup: your team needs a new captain. one player loudly says he deserves it; another quietly sets up the cones before every practice. what does Lehna's story point to?
options: the loud one; a captain has to want it and say so.
the one setting up cones; the unseen work counts.
neither; take a vote so it's fair to everyone.
fork.reveal: Lehna didn't campaign. he carried the wet grass. Guru Nanak placed the Guruship on the one doing the unseen work.

chat.meaning: Lehna became Guru Angad by doing work nobody photographed. Humility is sweetness and a low place, chosen; the unseen pots count.

Lehna.meaning: Guru Angad's name before he became the second Guru

Kartarpur.meaning: the town where Lehna came to serve Guru Nanak

Mata Khivi.meaning: Guru Angad's wife, remembered for her langar

kheer.meaning: rice cooked slowly in milk; a sweet pudding

Satta and Balvand.meaning: bards whose hymn about the Gurus is in the Granth
